prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 11.30. Exact Sanskrit: लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ताल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः ।
तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो ॥ ३० ॥ Exact stored meaning: O Viṣṇu! Licking all the worlds from every side with Your blazing mouths, You devour them. Your fierce radiances fill the entire universe, scorching it with their brilliance. Chapter context: The universal vision granted to Arjuna. Follow the verse-specific appearance, emotional response or prayer. Awe and cosmic scale, but no gore or graphic violence; when cosmic destruction is stated, use symbolic silhouettes and radiance. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: As moths rush with great speed into a blazing fire for their own destruction, so too do these creatures rush into Your mouths with great speed for their destruction. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Tell me — who are You in this fierce form? My salutations to You, O best among gods; be gracious. I wish to know You, the Primordial — for I do not comprehend Your activity (pravṛtti). Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 11.30: O Viṣṇu! Licking all the worlds from every side with Your blazing mouths, You devour them. Your fierce radiances fill the entire universe, scorching it with their brilliance.
